title: Can you recommend me movies with a similar vibe to Wong Kar Wai films?

commenti.body: [removed]
[removed]
Keep Cool (1997) by Zhang Yimou very consciously tries to go for the vibe of 90s Wong Kar-wai. It’s not a bad film, decent in its own right. One of the more overlooked titles in Zhang’s catalogue.

You might enjoy other films out of Hong Kong, I'd specifically recommend the early movies of Fruit Chan, as well as Johnnie To's peak period flicks from the late 90s to mid-2000s.

Some of Hsiao-Hsien Hou's films have a similar vibe, e.g. Millennium Mambo

And there are all the modern-day WKW ripoffs by Hollywood directors, e.g. Moonlight, Past Lives etc

Worth checking out the films of Bi Gan, particularly Kaili Blues, as well as the other films by the director of Suzhou River, Lou Ye - stuff like Saturday Fiction, Spring Fever, etc.

Wang Xiaoshuai also has a few films focused on specific Chinese cities - Shanghai Dreams, Chongqing Blues, and Beijing Bicycle.

On the Japanese side of things you could check out Adrift in Tokyo, too.
Thank you :)
For a Taiwanese equivalent of something like *As Tears Go By*, check out *Rebels of the Neon God*.
Thank you :)

Maybe give Tsai Ming-Liang a try. *Rebels of the Neon God* is really good.

Also, *Terrorizers*, and *Tapei Story* by Ed Yang. You'd probably like the rest of his movies too 

Ryusuke Hamaguchi is another favorite of mine, *Wheel of Fortune and Fantasy* and *Asako I&II* are both incredible

Can't help but recommend *Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives* as well, even though it's a bit on the slower side it has a lot of that aching, longing sensation you might find in *In the Mood for Love*, for example.

Also maybe check out *Portait of a Lady on Fire* if you haven't.... Kind of a random rec but it's really good and i think Wong Kar Wai fans would like it

Last rec.... Takeshi Kitano. Particularly his movie *A Scene at the Sea*. If you don't mind more action stuff, try *Violent Cop*, *Sonatine* (one of my favorite movies), and *Hana Bi*

You know what, I lied. For some reason i wanna recommend you Godard. I gotta see more Godard myself but check out *Breathless* and *Alphaville*
That's look like a very good list of interesting movies. Thank you

Takeshi Kitano is one of my favorite directors! My favorite film by this director is Kikujiro. After his brutal productions about Yakuza, I was surprised by how delicate and empathetic he could be towards the characters. He is an excellent artist.

Check out:

Yi Yi, a Taiwanese film from Edward Yang.

Shan He Gu Ren (Mountains may depart) by Jia Zhengke. He's one of the most famous mainland China directors and a lot of his movies scratch that Wong Kar Wai itch!
[removed]

I really enjoy [Comrades: Almost a Love Story](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117905/). It shares many of the same sensibilities of HK cinema and also stars Maggie Cheung. The cast also features Christopher Doyle, who coincidentally you may recognize as the director of photography (DP) on many of WKW's most notable movies including In the Mood For Love, Chunking Express, and Fallen Angels
Lost in Translation is tied for my favorite film of all time and I felt Wong Kar Wai's film "In the Mood for Love" was very close to it if not a bit better, so I'd say Lost in Translation
I just finished watching. A very good movie, thank you for the recommendation.

Yes. I think it's very underrated. You might also like *Goodbye, Dragon Inn*, which is much slower paced.

Have you explored much of Taiwanese cinema in general? Like *Yi Yi*?

Rebels of the Neon God was first Taiwanese movie I see in my life. 
I have been interested in East Asian cinema for less than a year and there is still a lot to discover when it comes to cinema from that region (including Taiwan).
